articles.detail: 5 cycles, 5 completed, avg 9.4/cycle; selections were 10/11/9/13/10 against targets of 11/12/13/15/15; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active (2026-10-03-odds-in-future-block was closed early today by the operator) and no pause gate is set. No new experiment: the science and tech shortfall is a second thin weekend day, matching the previous weekend (09-26/27: 5 and 3 science, 10 and 7 tech), and both writer and editor prompts plus a selector-facing pipeline commit changed today, so a baseline taken now would be confounded twice over.
weakestArea: Science plus tech is 15% against 25%, the lowest in the fortnight: science 2 (target 5) and politics 30 of 47 (64%). The cause is supply, not selection: in all five cycles the science feed was Scientific Reports manuscripts and thin Phys.org items with nothing from Nature, Quanta, New Scientist, STAT, SciDev.Net or Carbon Brief, and tech was under its floor after dedup in four cycles (0, 1, 0 and 1 against 3). Science under target on such a day is by design, but tech at 5 for two days running, after 13-15 on weekdays, is worth checking on Monday.
watching: Hormuz: Iran says the strait stays shut until seven conditions are met, with reopening within seven days if the US accepts.
OPEC+: ministers kept November output unchanged, covered in two pieces today, both leaning on TASS.
Iran: the foreign ministry confirmed discussions of withdrawing from the NPT, and the gas company admitted a drop in South Pars output; both are state-media only.
Russia and Ukraine: the Russian defence ministry vowed more strikes on Kyiv in response to Zelensky's refinery threats, sourced to TASS and RT alone.
US secondary sanctions on Russia's trade partners are due on 18 October.
Brazil voted in the first round for president, congress and governors; Bosnia's general election has preliminary results.
Yemen: the government declared an operation against the Houthis in al-Jawf.
North Korea claimed a hypersonic missile test over 1,000 km.
ASML's share move was flagged in two cycles with no story in the feed to explain it.
coverageGaps: Science has one source for the whole day (Phys.org) and two articles; the 05:00, 10:00 and 22:00 cycles published no science after dedup.
Tech published 0 in the 10:00 and 18:00 cycles; the Hacker News feed fell to 17-27 stories a cycle from 25-32 on weekdays.
Economy was under its floor after dedup in four of five cycles, and the feed had no multi-source economy story in three.
Eleven articles are sourced only from state or advocacy outlets, up from 3 yesterday, covering Iran, Russia, North Korea, Yemen, OPEC+ and the Brazilian and Bosnian elections.
TASS is a source on 9 of 47 articles (19%), one article short of the 20% limit, after 2-3 a day all week; counted by source entries it is 12, because one OPEC+ piece cites it four times.
Bloomberg thin picks were not recovered: full text was fetched for 1 of 8 thin sources across the day.
Freshness was measured on 6 of 47 articles, so the 0.4 median is indicative only.
context: A thin Sunday: all five cycles completed in an average of 796s (selector 181s, writer 151s, editor 64s) and the selector stopped short of its target in every cycle rather than pad, picking 53 against 66. Multi-source reached 55% (26 of 47), US datelines 19% and Latin America 9% on the Brazilian election, and all six regions appeared, so every goal but science and tech is met; the multi-source figure is helped by state-media pairs such as TASS plus RT, which count as two sources. If Monday and Tuesday feeds still carry no Nature, Quanta, STAT or Carbon Brief items, the next experiment should target science supply through CURATED_SOURCES, where those outlets are already listed, since the RSS list is off limits and the query cannot cost more NewsAPI tokens.
